title: Maximize Subarrays After Removing One Conflicting Pair
summary: Given an array nums containing the integers from 1 to n in order, and a 2D array conflictingPairs where each element [a, b] indicates a conflicting pair, remove exactly one conflicting pair from conflictingPairs.
statement: Given an array nums containing the integers from 1 to n in order, and a 2D array conflictingPairs where each element [a, b] indicates a conflicting pair, remove exactly one conflicting pair from conflictingPairs. Then, count the number of non-empty subarrays of nums that do not contain both elements of any remaining conflicting pair. Return the maximum number of such subarrays possible after removing one conflicting pair.
constraints: nums is implicitly [1,2,...,n], and conflicting_pairs is nonempty.
Count nonempty intervals [left,right] containing neither endpoint pair of every remaining conflict, and maximize that count.
hints: For each left endpoint, only the smallest and second-smallest conflicting right endpoints determine validity and the benefit of removing the active pair.
Sweep left endpoints backward while maintaining those two right boundaries and accumulate removal gains by the smallest boundary.
Add first-left to the base; add second-first to the gain bucket for first; return base plus the largest bucket.
Every invalid extension begins at the current smallest conflict, and removing that pair exposes exactly the second boundary until another left endpoint changes the limits.
editorial: Every invalid extension begins at the current smallest conflict, and removing that pair exposes exactly the second boundary until another left endpoint changes the limits.

tests.explanation: Removing the more restrictive pair permits nine valid subarrays.
Removing the only conflict makes all six nonempty subarrays valid.
